1	# ChronicleFlow
2	
3	ChronicleFlow is a small backend for durable workflow orchestration. It stores
4	workflow definitions, execution state, and an append-only event history in
5	SQLite so an execution can be inspected and replayed deterministically.
6	
7	The initial release intentionally supports a compact public contract:
8	
9	- workflows are directed acyclic graphs of `task`, `condition`, and bounded
10	  `loop` nodes;
11	- executions advance one ready task at a time, evaluating conditions and
12	  skipping unmatched branches automatically;
13	- task nodes may declare a bounded number of retries: a submitted failure
14	  re-queues the node until the retries are exhausted, which terminates the
15	  execution;
16	- executions may declare a timeout in seconds, after which they terminate and
17	  no longer accept output, and they may be cancelled explicitly;
18	- loop nodes repeat their body a bounded number of times, re-evaluating a
19	  continue condition at the loop boundaries;
20	- every state transition is appended to the execution event stream;
21	- replay rebuilds execution state from the recorded events;
22	- a checkpoint is written at every node boundary, capturing the state
23	  summary and event position, so an execution can be recovered from the
24	  latest checkpoint after a restart;
25	- workers may claim a running execution to receive a work item with a
26	  time-bounded lease, renew the lease with heartbeats, and release it;
27	  while a lease is active only its holder may submit results, and an
28	  expired or released lease returns the work item to the claimable set;
29	- duplicate commands with the same idempotency key return the original result.
30	
31	## Requirements
32	
33	- Python 3.11 or newer
34	- no third-party runtime dependencies
35	
36	## Run the service
37	
38	```bash
39	PYTHONPATH=src python -m chronicleflow.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --database chronicleflow.db
40	```
41	
42	The process prints `ChronicleFlow listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080` after it
43	has bound the port.
44	
45	## HTTP API
46	
47	All request and response bodies are JSON. Unknown fields are rejected.
48	
49	### Health
50	
51	```http
52	GET /health
53	```
54	
55	Returns `{"status":"ok"}`.
56	
57	### Create a workflow
58	
59	```http
60	POST /workflows
61	Idempotency-Key: workflow-request-1
62	
63	{
64	  "id": "order-flow",
65	  "nodes": [
66	    {"id": "reserve", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
67	    {"id": "charge", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["reserve"]}
68	  ]
69	}
70	```
71	
72	Returns HTTP 201 with the stored workflow. Node identifiers must be unique,
73	dependencies must exist, and cycles are rejected.
74	
75	Besides `task`, a node may have `kind` set to `condition`:
76	
77	```json
78	{"id": "is_vip", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": ["reserve"], "path": "customer.vip", "equals": true}
79	```
80	
81	`path` is a non-empty dot-separated path into the execution input and `equals`
82	is a JSON scalar (string, number, boolean, or null). A condition is evaluated
83	automatically once its dependencies complete: the input value at `path` is
84	compared with `equals` by JSON type and value, and a missing path evaluates to
85	`false`.
86	
87	A task may carry an optional `run_if` guard:
88	
89	```json
90	{"id": "expedite", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["is_vip"], "run_if": {"condition_id": "is_vip", "expected": true}}
91	```
92	
93	`condition_id` must reference a `condition` node that is also listed in the
94	task's `depends_on`. When the condition's result differs from `expected`, the
95	task is marked as skipped: it receives no output and still satisfies the
96	dependencies of its successors.
97	
98	A task may declare how many times it is retried after a failure:
99	
100	```json
101	{"id": "charge", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["reserve"], "retries": 3}
102	```
103	
104	`retries` is an integer between 0 and 10 and defaults to 0, meaning the task
105	is attempted only once. Each failure submitted through `advance` consumes one
106	attempt; while retries remain, the task returns to the ready set and is
107	advanced again. When a failure arrives with no retries left, the task is
108	permanently failed and the whole execution terminates with termination reason
109	`retries_exhausted`.
110	
111	A node may also have `kind` set to `loop`, describing a bounded repeated
112	segment:
113	
114	```json
115	{"id": "retry", "kind": "loop", "depends_on": ["reserve"], "entry": "attempt", "condition": "keep_trying", "max_iterations": 3}
116	```
117	
118	A loop node contains exactly `id`, `kind`, `depends_on`, `entry`, `condition`,
119	and `max_iterations`; any other field is rejected as unknown. `entry` names a
120	`task` node, `condition` names a `condition` node, and `max_iterations` is an
121	integer between 1 and 100. The loop body is the entry task plus every node
122	reachable from it through `depends_on`; the body keeps the usual DAG rules and
123	must contain the referenced condition. The loop's own dependencies must be
124	completed or skipped before the first iteration may start, they must not
125	overlap the body, bodies of different loops must not overlap or nest, and
126	nodes outside a body must not depend on nodes inside it (they depend on the
127	loop node instead).
128	
129	When the loop's dependencies are satisfied, the loop evaluates its condition
130	against the execution input (same JSON type and value comparison as condition
131	nodes; a missing path is `false`). If it is `false`, the loop completes with
132	zero iterations and end reason `condition_false`. If it is `true`, the first
133	iteration starts and the body advances one ready task per `advance` call in
134	the usual deterministic order; conditions and `run_if` skips inside the body
135	are re-evaluated every iteration, and task outputs belong only to the current
136	iteration. Once every body node is completed or skipped, the condition is
137	evaluated again: `true` starts the next iteration, `false` ends the loop with
138	`condition_false`, and reaching `max_iterations` ends it with
139	`iteration_limit` after that iteration finishes. Ending the loop completes
140	the loop node and releases the dependencies of its successors.
141	
142	Execution state exposes each loop under `loops`: `status`, the
143	`current_iteration`, one entry per iteration with its own `completed_nodes`,
144	`skipped_nodes`, `condition_results`, and `outputs`, and the single
145	`end_reason` (`condition_false` or `iteration_limit`). The event stream
146	records `iteration_started`, `loop_condition_evaluated`, and `loop_completed`
147	events alongside the usual per-node ones, so replay rebuilds loop state
148	exactly.
149	
150	### Start an execution
151	
152	```http
153	POST /executions
154	Idempotency-Key: execution-request-1
155	
156	{"id":"run-1","workflow_id":"order-flow","input":{"order_id":"o-7"}}
157	```
158	
159	Returns HTTP 201. The execution starts in `running` state.
160	
161	An execution may declare a timeout:
162	
163	```json
164	{"id":"run-2","workflow_id":"order-flow","input":{},"timeout_seconds":30}
165	```
166	
167	`timeout_seconds` is a positive number of seconds counted from the moment the
168	execution starts. Once the deadline passes, the execution terminates with
169	termination reason `timeout` and no longer accepts output. Executions without
170	a timeout never expire.
171	
172	### Inspect an execution
173	
174	```http
175	GET /executions/run-1
176	GET /executions/run-1/events
177	GET /executions/run-1/checkpoints
178	```
179	
180	The first endpoint returns the materialized state. The second returns the
181	ordered event stream. The third returns the ordered checkpoints; each entry
182	gives its `sequence`, the `event_sequence` position it was taken at, the full
183	`state` summary, and `created_at`.
184	
185	### Checkpoints
186	
187	Every successful `advance` that settles a node boundary — a task is
188	completed, or a failure is submitted (whether it retries or exhausts the
189	attempts) — writes a checkpoint in the same transaction as the state update
190	and event append. The checkpoint stores the complete state summary at that
191	boundary, including completed, skipped, and failed nodes, condition results,
192	outputs, attempts with their unfinished retry counts, and the status and
193	current iteration of every loop (with the per-iteration records), together
194	with the position of the last written event. Because the checkpoint matches
195	the stored state at that position, recovery can continue without replaying or
196	duplicating any node output.
197	
198	Checkpoints do not add fields to the execution state and do not append events:
199	an execution that declares no retries, timeout, or loops keeps exactly the
200	same state shape and event stream as before.
201	
202	### Complete the next ready node
203	
204	```http
205	POST /executions/run-1/advance
206	Idempotency-Key: advance-request-1
207	
208	{"output":{"reservation_id":"r-9"}}
209	```
210	
211	The lexicographically first ready task is completed. The response contains the
212	updated execution. Before that, each call first evaluates all ready conditions
213	in deterministic order and skips tasks whose `run_if` does not match; if this
214	automatic processing finishes the execution, the current state is returned and
215	the submitted output is not consumed. When every node is completed or skipped,
216	the status becomes `completed`.
217	
218	Instead of an output, a failure can be submitted for the same ready task:
219	
220	```http
221	POST /executions/run-1/advance
222	Idempotency-Key: advance-request-2
223	
224	{"failure":{"reason":"gateway timeout"}}
225	```
226	
227	The body must contain exactly one of `output` or `failure`, and `failure`
228	carries exactly a `reason` string. Either body may additionally carry a
229	`worker_id` string identifying the lease holder when the execution's work
230	item has been claimed (see "Claim a work item"). A failed task appends a `node_failed`
231	event recording the attempt number and reason. While the task has retries
232	left it returns to the ready set and a `node_retried` event records the next
233	attempt number; otherwise the task is permanently failed and the execution
234	terminates with reason `retries_exhausted`. The same rules apply to tasks
235	inside loop bodies, which are retried within their current iteration.
236	
237	Execution state includes `completed_nodes` (which also lists evaluated
238	conditions), `skipped_nodes`, `failed_nodes`, `condition_results`, `outputs`,
239	and `attempts`. `attempts` maps each attempted task to its current `attempt`
240	number and its `failures` count; loop body tasks track the same per iteration.
241	Each condition evaluation appends a `condition_evaluated` event and each skip
242	a `node_skipped` event to the execution stream.
243	
244	### Cancel an execution
245	
246	```http
247	POST /executions/run-1/cancel
248	Idempotency-Key: cancel-request-1
249	```
250	
251	A running execution is terminated immediately with termination reason
252	`cancelled`. Cancelling a completed or already terminated execution returns
253	its state unchanged, and cancelling a missing execution returns 404.
254	
255	Execution status is `running`, `completed`, or `terminated`. A terminated
256	execution records exactly one `termination_reason` — `retries_exhausted`,
257	`timeout`, or `cancelled` — and appends a single `execution_terminated`
258	event; completed executions keep a `null` termination reason and their own
259	`execution_completed` event. Advancing a terminated execution returns its
260	state unchanged without consuming the submitted output or failure.
261	
262	### Claim a work item
263	
264	```http
265	POST /executions/run-1/claim
266	Idempotency-Key: claim-request-1
267	
268	{"worker_id":"worker-7","lease_seconds":30}
269	```
270	
271	Claiming is how an external worker takes ownership of a running execution
272	before advancing its ready tasks. `worker_id` is a non-empty string and
273	`lease_seconds` is an optional positive number of seconds (default 30). The
274	response contains the claimed `work_item` (its `execution_id` and
275	`workflow_id`) and a `lease` recording the `worker_id`, the `lease_seconds`
276	duration, the `expires_at` deadline, and the `heartbeat_at` active time.
277	Each work item is held by at most one worker at a time: claiming a work
278	item whose lease is still active — even by the same worker — is a 409
279	`conflict`. Claiming a completed or terminated execution returns the
280	definite empty result `{"work_item":null,"lease":null}` and absorbs no
281	input, and claiming a missing execution returns 404.
282	
283	While a work item is held, results are submitted through the usual
284	`advance` entry by including the holder's identity:
285	
286	```http
287	POST /executions/run-1/advance
288	Idempotency-Key: advance-request-3
289	
290	{"output":{"reservation_id":"r-9"},"worker_id":"worker-7"}
291	```
292	
293	Submitting results for a work item held by another worker, or after the
294	lease has expired, is a 409 `conflict` that does not change execution
295	state. An execution that never claimed a work item accepts `advance`
296	exactly as before, and its state fields and event stream are identical to
297	an execution without any claim.
298	
299	When a lease expires, the work item returns to the claimable set and may be
300	claimed again by the same or another worker. The second claim continues
301	from the materialized state: node outputs and results recorded by the
302	earlier holder are never advanced or recorded twice, and every written
303	output belongs to the single advance that submitted it.
304	
305	### Renew a lease
306	
307	```http
308	POST /executions/run-1/heartbeat
309	Idempotency-Key: heartbeat-request-1
310	
311	{"worker_id":"worker-7"}
312	```
313	
314	Within the lease period the holder may heartbeat to extend `expires_at` by
315	the lease duration and refresh the `heartbeat_at` active time; the response
316	carries the updated `lease`. A heartbeat never advances nodes, writes
317	outputs, or appends node events. A heartbeat from another worker or after
318	the lease expired is a 409 `conflict`; a heartbeat for a missing execution
319	or an execution with no claimed work item is a 404 `not_found`.
320	
321	### Release a work item
322	
323	```http
324	POST /executions/run-1/release
325	Idempotency-Key: release-request-1
326	
327	{"worker_id":"worker-7"}
328	```
329	
330	Releasing invalidates the lease immediately and returns the work item to
331	the claimable set, so it can be claimed again right away; progress already
332	made and the recorded events are unchanged. Releasing with another
333	worker's identity or after expiry is a 409 `conflict`; releasing for a
334	missing execution or an execution with no claimed work item is a 404
335	`not_found`.
336	
337	Claims, heartbeats, and releases append no events and add no fields to the
338	execution state, so replay, checkpoints, and recovery are unaffected.
339	Leases live in the same SQLite database as the execution state, so
340	unexpired leases and claim ownership remain valid after the service
341	restarts.
342	
343	### Recover from a checkpoint
344	
345	```http
346	POST /executions/run-1/recover
347	Idempotency-Key: recover-request-1
348	
349	{"from":"latest_checkpoint"}
350	```
351	
352	Recovery rebuilds a running execution from its latest checkpoint and returns
353	the rebuilt execution. It appends no events and changes no state: the rebuilt
354	execution is exactly the materialized state, and a subsequent replay has the
355	same conclusion as before the interruption. After recovery, further
356	`advance` calls continue from the checkpoint, so node outputs, failure
357	reasons, attempt numbers, and loop iteration ownership are identical to an
358	uninterrupted run; failure records for tasks inside a loop body still carry
359	their loop id and current iteration. Recovery works after the service has
360	been restarted, because checkpoints live in the same SQLite database as the
361	execution state and events.
362	
363	A completed execution is returned unchanged, producing no new events. A
364	terminated execution is likewise returned unchanged and the operation
365	absorbs no input; if a timeout or cancellation takes effect between
366	checkpoint writes, termination takes precedence over recovery. Events and
367	checkpoints remain queryable after cancellation or timeout, and their replay
368	stays consistent with the materialized state.
369	
370	Recovering a missing execution returns 404. Recovering an execution that has
371	no checkpoint, or whose latest checkpoint cannot be parsed, returns 409
372	`conflict`. A missing `from` field, a wrong type, or an unknown recovery
373	origin is a 400 `validation_error`; a non-finite number in the body is
374	rejected the same way as every other request. Reusing an idempotency key
375	already used by another operation (including an `advance` or `cancel` on the
376	same execution) returns 409 `conflict`.
377	
378	### Replay
379	
380	```http
381	POST /executions/run-1/replay
382	```
383	
384	Rebuilds state solely from the execution event stream and compares it with the
385	stored materialized state. A successful response contains `consistent: true`
386	and the rebuilt execution.
387	
388	## Errors
389	
390	Errors use this shape:
391	
392	```json
393	{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"human readable detail"}}
394	```
395	
396	Validation errors return 400, missing resources return 404, and conflicts
397	return 409. A `retries` value that is negative, non-integer, or greater than
398	10, and a non-positive `timeout_seconds`, are validation errors. Reusing a
399	workflow or execution identifier, or reusing an idempotency key across
400	different operations, is a conflict. Claiming a work item whose lease is
401	still active, submitting results for a work item held by another worker or
402	after the lease expired, and heartbeating or releasing a lease held by
403	another worker are conflicts, while heartbeating or releasing an execution
404	with no claimed work item is a missing resource. Recovering a missing
405	execution is a missing resource, while recovering an execution that has no
406	checkpoint or whose latest checkpoint is unparseable is a conflict; an
407	invalid recover body is a validation error. Request bodies must not contain
408	non-finite numbers (`NaN`, `Infinity`, or overflowing values such as `1e400`);
409	they are rejected with 400. Finite floats keep their full precision, including negative zero
410	(`-0.0`), and every response body ends with a single newline.
411	
412	## Tests
413	
414	```bash
415	PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
416	```
417

- executions advance one ready task at a time, evaluating conditions and
  skipping unmatched branches automatically;
- task nodes may declare a bounded number of retries: a submitted failure
  re-queues the node until the retries are exhausted, which terminates the
  execution;
- executions may declare a timeout in seconds, after which they terminate and
  no longer accept output, and they may be cancelled explicitly;
- loop nodes repeat their body a bounded number of times, re-evaluating a
  continue condition at the loop boundaries;
- every state transition is appended to the execution event stream;
- replay rebuilds execution state from the recorded events;
- a checkpoint is written at every node boundary, capturing the state
  summary and event position, so an execution can be recovered from the
  latest checkpoint after a restart;
- workers may claim a running execution to receive a work item with a
  time-bounded lease, renew the lease with heartbeats, and release it;
  while a lease is active only its holder may submit results, and an
  expired or released lease returns the work item to the claimable set;
- duplicate commands with the same idempotency key return the original result.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11 or newer
- no third-party runtime dependencies

## Run the service

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m chronicleflow.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --database chronicleflow.db
```

The process prints `ChronicleFlow listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080` after it
has bound the port.

## HTTP API

All request and response bodies are JSON. Unknown fields are rejected.

### Health

```http
GET /health
```

Returns `{"status":"ok"}`.

### Create a workflow

```http
POST /workflows
Idempotency-Key: workflow-request-1

{
  "id": "order-flow",
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "reserve", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
    {"id": "charge", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["reserve"]}
  ]
}
```

Returns HTTP 201 with the stored workflow. Node identifiers must be unique,
dependencies must exist, and cycles are rejected.

Besides `task`, a node may have `kind` set to `condition`:

```json
{"id": "is_vip", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": ["reserve"], "path": "customer.vip", "equals": true}
```

`path` is a non-empty dot-separated path into the execution input and `equals`
is a JSON scalar (string, number, boolean, or null). A condition is evaluated
automatically once its dependencies complete: the input value at `path` is
compared with `equals` by JSON type and value, and a missing path evaluates to
`false`.

A task may carry an optional `run_if` guard:

```json
{"id": "expedite", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["is_vip"], "run_if": {"condition_id": "is_vip", "expected": true}}
```

`condition_id` must reference a `condition` node that is also listed in the
task's `depends_on`. When the condition's result differs from `expected`, the
task is marked as skipped: it receives no output and still satisfies the
dependencies of its successors.

A task may declare how many times it is retried after a failure:

```json
{"id": "charge", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["reserve"], "retries": 3}
```

`retries` is an integer between 0 and 10 and defaults to 0, meaning the task
is attempted only once. Each failure submitted through `advance` consumes one
attempt; while retries remain, the task returns to the ready set and is
advanced again. When a failure arrives with no retries left, the task is
permanently failed and the whole execution terminates with termination reason
`retries_exhausted`.

A node may also have `kind` set to `loop`, describing a bounded repeated
segment:

```json
{"id": "retry", "kind": "loop", "depends_on": ["reserve"], "entry": "attempt", "condition": "keep_trying", "max_iterations": 3}
```

A loop node contains exactly `id`, `kind`, `depends_on`, `entry`, `condition`,
and `max_iterations`; any other field is rejected as unknown. `entry` names a
`task` node, `condition` names a `condition` node, and `max_iterations` is an
integer between 1 and 100. The loop body is the entry task plus every node
reachable from it through `depends_on`; the body keeps the usual DAG rules and
must contain the referenced condition. The loop's own dependencies must be
completed or skipped before the first iteration may start, they must not
overlap the body, bodies of different loops must not overlap or nest, and
nodes outside a body must not depend on nodes inside it (they depend on the
loop node instead).

When the loop's dependencies are satisfied, the loop evaluates its condition
against the execution input (same JSON type and value comparison as condition
nodes; a missing path is `false`). If it is `false`, the loop completes with
zero iterations and end reason `condition_false`. If it is `true`, the first
iteration starts and the body advances one ready task per `advance` call in
the usual deterministic order; conditions and `run_if` skips inside the body
are re-evaluated every iteration, and task outputs belong only to the current
iteration. Once every body node is completed or skipped, the condition is
evaluated again: `true` starts the next iteration, `false` ends the loop with
`condition_false`, and reaching `max_iterations` ends it with
`iteration_limit` after that iteration finishes. Ending the loop completes
the loop node and releases the dependencies of its successors.

Execution state exposes each loop under `loops`: `status`, the
`current_iteration`, one entry per iteration with its own `completed_nodes`,
`skipped_nodes`, `condition_results`, and `outputs`, and the single
`end_reason` (`condition_false` or `iteration_limit`). The event stream
records `iteration_started`, `loop_condition_evaluated`, and `loop_completed`
events alongside the usual per-node ones, so replay rebuilds loop state
exactly.

### Start an execution

```http
POST /executions
Idempotency-Key: execution-request-1

{"id":"run-1","workflow_id":"order-flow","input":{"order_id":"o-7"}}
```

Returns HTTP 201. The execution starts in `running` state.

An execution may declare a timeout:

```json
{"id":"run-2","workflow_id":"order-flow","input":{},"timeout_seconds":30}
```

`timeout_seconds` is a positive number of seconds counted from the moment the
execution starts. Once the deadline passes, the execution terminates with
termination reason `timeout` and no longer accepts output. Executions without
a timeout never expire.

### Inspect an execution

```http
GET /executions/run-1
GET /executions/run-1/events
GET /executions/run-1/checkpoints
```

The first endpoint returns the materialized state. The second returns the
ordered event stream. The third returns the ordered checkpoints; each entry
gives its `sequence`, the `event_sequence` position it was taken at, the full
`state` summary, and `created_at`.

### Checkpoints

Every successful `advance` that settles a node boundary — a task is
completed, or a failure is submitted (whether it retries or exhausts the
attempts) — writes a checkpoint in the same transaction as the state update
and event append. The checkpoint stores the complete state summary at that
boundary, including completed, skipped, and failed nodes, condition results,
outputs, attempts with their unfinished retry counts, and the status and
current iteration of every loop (with the per-iteration records), together
with the position of the last written event. Because the checkpoint matches
the stored state at that position, recovery can continue without replaying or
duplicating any node output.

Checkpoints do not add fields to the execution state and do not append events:
an execution that declares no retries, timeout, or loops keeps exactly the
same state shape and event stream as before.

### Complete the next ready node

```http
POST /executions/run-1/advance
Idempotency-Key: advance-request-1

{"output":{"reservation_id":"r-9"}}
```

The lexicographically first ready task is completed. The response contains the
updated execution. Before that, each call first evaluates all ready conditions
in deterministic order and skips tasks whose `run_if` does not match; if this
automatic processing finishes the execution, the current state is returned and
the submitted output is not consumed. When every node is completed or skipped,
the status becomes `completed`.

Instead of an output, a failure can be submitted for the same ready task:

```http
POST /executions/run-1/advance
Idempotency-Key: advance-request-2

{"failure":{"reason":"gateway timeout"}}
```

The body must contain exactly one of `output` or `failure`, and `failure`
carries exactly a `reason` string. Either body may additionally carry a
`worker_id` string identifying the lease holder when the execution's work
item has been claimed (see "Claim a work item"). A failed task appends a `node_failed`
event recording the attempt number and reason. While the task has retries
left it returns to the ready set and a `node_retried` event records the next
attempt number; otherwise the task is permanently failed and the execution
terminates with reason `retries_exhausted`. The same rules apply to tasks
inside loop bodies, which are retried within their current iteration.

Execution state includes `completed_nodes` (which also lists evaluated
conditions), `skipped_nodes`, `failed_nodes`, `condition_results`, `outputs`,
and `attempts`. `attempts` maps each attempted task to its current `attempt`
number and its `failures` count; loop body tasks track the same per iteration.
Each condition evaluation appends a `condition_evaluated` event and each skip
a `node_skipped` event to the execution stream.

### Cancel an execution

```http
POST /executions/run-1/cancel
Idempotency-Key: cancel-request-1
```

A running execution is terminated immediately with termination reason
`cancelled`. Cancelling a completed or already terminated execution returns
its state unchanged, and cancelling a missing execution returns 404.

Execution status is `running`, `completed`, or `terminated`. A terminated
execution records exactly one `termination_reason` — `retries_exhausted`,
`timeout`, or `cancelled` — and appends a single `execution_terminated`
event; completed executions keep a `null` termination reason and their own
`execution_completed` event. Advancing a terminated execution returns its
state unchanged without consuming the submitted output or failure.

### Claim a work item

```http
POST /executions/run-1/claim
Idempotency-Key: claim-request-1

{"worker_id":"worker-7","lease_seconds":30}
```

Claiming is how an external worker takes ownership of a running execution
before advancing its ready tasks. `worker_id` is a non-empty string and
`lease_seconds` is an optional positive number of seconds (default 30). The
response contains the claimed `work_item` (its `execution_id` and
`workflow_id`) and a `lease` recording the `worker_id`, the `lease_seconds`
duration, the `expires_at` deadline, and the `heartbeat_at` active time.
Each work item is held by at most one worker at a time: claiming a work
item whose lease is still active — even by the same worker — is a 409
`conflict`. Claiming a completed or terminated execution returns the
definite empty result `{"work_item":null,"lease":null}` and absorbs no
input, and claiming a missing execution returns 404.

While a work item is held, results are submitted through the usual
`advance` entry by including the holder's identity:

```http
POST /executions/run-1/advance
Idempotency-Key: advance-request-3

{"output":{"reservation_id":"r-9"},"worker_id":"worker-7"}
```

Submitting results for a work item held by another worker, or after the
lease has expired, is a 409 `conflict` that does not change execution
state. An execution that never claimed a work item accepts `advance`
exactly as before, and its state fields and event stream are identical to
an execution without any claim.

When a lease expires, the work item returns to the claimable set and may be
claimed again by the same or another worker. The second claim continues
from the materialized state: node outputs and results recorded by the
earlier holder are never advanced or recorded twice, and every written
output belongs to the single advance that submitted it.

### Renew a lease

```http
POST /executions/run-1/heartbeat
Idempotency-Key: heartbeat-request-1

{"worker_id":"worker-7"}
```

Within the lease period the holder may heartbeat to extend `expires_at` by
the lease duration and refresh the `heartbeat_at` active time; the response
carries the updated `lease`. A heartbeat never advances nodes, writes
outputs, or appends node events. A heartbeat from another worker or after
the lease expired is a 409 `conflict`; a heartbeat for a missing execution
or an execution with no claimed work item is a 404 `not_found`.

### Release a work item

```http
POST /executions/run-1/release
Idempotency-Key: release-request-1

{"worker_id":"worker-7"}
```

Releasing invalidates the lease immediately and returns the work item to
the claimable set, so it can be claimed again right away; progress already
made and the recorded events are unchanged. Releasing with another
worker's identity or after expiry is a 409 `conflict`; releasing for a
missing execution or an execution with no claimed work item is a 404
`not_found`.

Claims, heartbeats, and releases append no events and add no fields to the
execution state, so replay, checkpoints, and recovery are unaffected.
Leases live in the same SQLite database as the execution state, so
unexpired leases and claim ownership remain valid after the service
restarts.

### Recover from a checkpoint

```http
POST /executions/run-1/recover
Idempotency-Key: recover-request-1

{"from":"latest_checkpoint"}
```

Recovery rebuilds a running execution from its latest checkpoint and returns
the rebuilt execution. It appends no events and changes no state: the rebuilt
execution is exactly the materialized state, and a subsequent replay has the
same conclusion as before the interruption. After recovery, further
`advance` calls continue from the checkpoint, so node outputs, failure
reasons, attempt numbers, and loop iteration ownership are identical to an
uninterrupted run; failure records for tasks inside a loop body still carry
their loop id and current iteration. Recovery works after the service has
been restarted, because checkpoints live in the same SQLite database as the
execution state and events.

A completed execution is returned unchanged, producing no new events. A
terminated execution is likewise returned unchanged and the operation
absorbs no input; if a timeout or cancellation takes effect between
checkpoint writes, termination takes precedence over recovery. Events and
checkpoints remain queryable after cancellation or timeout, and their replay
stays consistent with the materialized state.

Recovering a missing execution returns 404. Recovering an execution that has
no checkpoint, or whose latest checkpoint cannot be parsed, returns 409
`conflict`. A missing `from` field, a wrong type, or an unknown recovery
origin is a 400 `validation_error`; a non-finite number in the body is
rejected the same way as every other request. Reusing an idempotency key
already used by another operation (including an `advance` or `cancel` on the
same execution) returns 409 `conflict`.

### Replay

```http
POST /executions/run-1/replay
```

Rebuilds state solely from the execution event stream and compares it with the
stored materialized state. A successful response contains `consistent: true`
and the rebuilt execution.

## Errors

Errors use this shape:

```json
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"human readable detail"}}
```

Validation errors return 400, missing resources return 404, and conflicts
return 409. A `retries` value that is negative, non-integer, or greater than
10, and a non-positive `timeout_seconds`, are validation errors. Reusing a
workflow or execution identifier, or reusing an idempotency key across
different operations, is a conflict. Claiming a work item whose lease is
still active, submitting results for a work item held by another worker or
after the lease expired, and heartbeating or releasing a lease held by
another worker are conflicts, while heartbeating or releasing an execution
with no claimed work item is a missing resource. Recovering a missing
execution is a missing resource, while recovering an execution that has no
checkpoint or whose latest checkpoint is unparseable is a conflict; an
invalid recover body is a validation error. Request bodies must not contain
non-finite numbers (`NaN`, `Infinity`, or overflowing values such as `1e400`);
they are rejected with 400. Finite floats keep their full precision, including negative zero
(`-0.0`), and every response body ends with a single newline.

## Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

219	            raise ValidationError(f"loop {node.id} entry must not depend on the loop itself")
220	        if any(by_id[member].kind == "loop" for member in body):
221	            raise ValidationError(f"loop {node.id} body must not contain another loop")
222	        judge = by_id.get(node.condition)
223	        if judge is None:
224	            raise ValidationError(f"loop {node.id} condition references an unknown node")
225	        if judge.kind != "condition":
226	            raise ValidationError(f"loop {node.id} condition must reference a condition node")
227	        if judge.id not in body:
228	            raise ValidationError(f"loop {node.id} condition must belong to the loop body")
229	        bodies[node.id] = body
230	    owner: dict[str, str] = {}
231	    for loop_id, body in bodies.items():
232	        for member in body:
233	            if member in owner:
234	                raise ValidationError(f"node {member} belongs to more than one loop body")
235	            owner[member] = loop_id
236	    for node in nodes:
237	        if node.id in owner:
238	            continue
239	        for dependency in node.depends_on:
240	            if dependency in owner:
241	                raise ValidationError(
242	                    f"node {node.id} must not depend on loop body node {dependency}; depend on loop {owner[dependency]} instead"
243	                )
244	
245	
246	def _assert_acyclic(nodes: tuple[Node, ...]) -> None:
247	    graph = {node.id: node.depends_on for node in nodes}
248	    visiting: set[str] = set()
249	    visited: set[str] = set()
250	
251	    def visit(node_id: str) -> None:
252	        if node_id in visiting:
253	            raise ValidationError("workflow contains a dependency cycle")
254	        if node_id in visited:
255	            return
256	        visiting.add(node_id)
257	        for dependency in graph[node_id]:
258	            visit(dependency)
259	        visiting.remove(node_id)
260	        visited.add(node_id)
261	
262	    for node_id in graph:
263	        visit(node_id)

48	    def _idempotent(self, key: str | None, operation: str, action: Callable[[], dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
49	        if not key:
50	            raise ValidationError("Idempotency-Key header is required")
51	        with self.store.transaction() as connection:
52	            existing = connection.execute("SELECT operation, response FROM idempotency WHERE key = ?", (key,)).fetchone()
53	            if existing:
54	                if existing["operation"] != operation:
55	                    raise ConflictError("idempotency key was already used for another operation")
56	                return self.store.decode(existing["response"])
57	            response = action()
58	            connection.execute(
59	                "INSERT INTO idempotency(key, operation, response) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
60	                (key, operation, self.store.encode(response)),
61	            )
62	            return response

178	            {"output"},
179	            {"failure"},

201	            workflow_row = self.store.connection.execute("SELECT document FROM workflows WHERE id = ?", (state["workflow_id"],)).fetchone()

240	    @staticmethod
241	    def _lease_payload(worker_id: str, lease_seconds: float, expires_at: float, heartbeat_at: float) -> dict[str, Any]:

249	    def _assert_submission_allowed(self, execution_id: str, worker_id: str | None) -> None:
250	        """Once a work item is claimed, only the active lease holder may submit results."""
251	        row = self._lease_row(execution_id)
252	        if row is None:
253	            return
254	        if time.time() >= row["expires_at"]:
255	            raise ConflictError(f"lease for execution {execution_id} has expired")
256	        if worker_id != row["worker_id"]:
257	            raise ConflictError(f"work item for execution {execution_id} is held by another worker")

259	    def claim(self, execution_id: str, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
260	        if not isinstance(raw, dict) or "worker_id" not in raw or not set(raw) <= {"worker_id", "lease_seconds"}:
261	            raise ValidationError("claim body must contain a worker_id and optionally lease_seconds")
262	        worker_id = _identifier(raw["worker_id"], "worker id")
263	        lease_seconds = raw.get("lease_seconds", DEFAULT_LEASE_SECONDS)
264	        if isinstance(lease_seconds, bool) or not isinstance(lease_seconds, (int, float)):
265	            raise ValidationError("lease_seconds must be a positive number of seconds")
266	        if not math.isfinite(lease_seconds) or lease_seconds <= 0:
267	            raise ValidationError("lease_seconds must be a positive number of seconds")
268	
269	        def apply() -> dict[str, Any]:
270	            state = self.get_execution(execution_id)
271	            if state["status"] != "running":
272	                # A finished execution has no claimable work item; the request
273	                # is a definite empty result and absorbs no input.
274	                return {"work_item": None, "lease": None}
275	            now = time.time()
276	            row = self._lease_row(execution_id)
277	            if row is not None and now < row["expires_at"]:
278	                raise ConflictError(f"work item for execution {execution_id} is already claimed")
279	            expires_at = now + lease_seconds
280	            self.store.connection.execute(
281	                "INSERT INTO leases(execution_id, worker_id, lease_seconds, expires_at, heartbeat_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?) "
282	                "ON CONFLICT(execution_id) DO UPDATE SET worker_id = excluded.worker_id, "
283	                "lease_seconds = excluded.lease_seconds, expires_at = excluded.expires_at, heartbeat_at = excluded.heartbeat_at",
284	                (execution_id, worker_id, lease_seconds, expires_at, now),
285	            )
286	            return {
287	                "work_item": {"execution_id": execution_id, "workflow_id": state["workflow_id"]},
288	                "lease": self._lease_payload(worker_id, lease_seconds, expires_at, now),
289	            }
290	
291	        return self._idempotent(key, f"claim:{execution_id}", apply)

293	    def heartbeat(self, execution_id: str, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
294	        if not isinstance(raw, dict) or set(raw) != {"worker_id"}:
295	            raise ValidationError("heartbeat body must contain exactly a worker_id")
296	        worker_id = _identifier(raw["worker_id"], "worker id")
297	
298	        def apply() -> dict[str, Any]:
299	            state = self.get_execution(execution_id)
300	            row = self._lease_row(execution_id)
301	            if row is None:
302	                raise NotFoundError(f"execution {execution_id} has no claimed work item")
303	            now = time.time()
304	            if state["status"] != "running":
305	                raise ConflictError(f"execution {execution_id} is not running")
306	            if now >= row["expires_at"]:
307	                raise ConflictError(f"lease for execution {execution_id} has expired")
308	            if row["worker_id"] != worker_id:
309	                raise ConflictError(f"work item for execution {execution_id} is held by another worker")
310	            # A heartbeat only extends the lease and refreshes the active time;
311	            # it never advances nodes, writes outputs, or appends node events.
312	            expires_at = now + row["lease_seconds"]
313	            self.store.connection.execute(
314	                "UPDATE leases SET expires_at = ?, heartbeat_at = ? WHERE execution_id = ?",
315	                (expires_at, now, execution_id),
316	            )
317	            return {"lease": self._lease_payload(worker_id, row["lease_seconds"], expires_at, now)}
318	
319	        return self._idempotent(key, f"heartbeat:{execution_id}", apply)

358	    def recover(self, execution_id: str, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
359	        if not isinstance(raw, dict) or set(raw) != {"from"} or not isinstance(raw["from"], str):
360	            raise ValidationError("recover body must contain exactly a from string")
361	        if raw["from"] != "latest_checkpoint":

368	            if state["status"] != "running":
369	                return state

380	            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as error:
381	                raise ConflictError("latest checkpoint is not parseable") from error
382	            if not isinstance(snapshot, dict) or not isinstance(event_sequence, int):
383	                raise ConflictError("latest checkpoint is not parseable")
384	            if snapshot != state:

390	    def _node_container(self, workflow: Workflow, state: dict[str, Any], node_id: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
391	        """Return the state fragment holding the node's progress and its event context."""
392	        loop_id = self._active_loop(workflow, state, node_id)
393	        if loop_id is None:
394	            return state, {}
395	        loop_state = state["loops"][loop_id]
396	        return loop_state["iterations"][-1], {"loop_id": loop_id, "iteration": loop_state["current_iteration"]}

398	    def _complete_node(self, execution_id: str, workflow: Workflow, state: dict[str, Any], node_id: str, output: Any) -> None:
399	        container, context = self._node_container(workflow, state, node_id)
400	        container["completed_nodes"].append(node_id)
401	        container["outputs"][node_id] = output
402	        container["attempts"].setdefault(node_id, {"attempt": 1, "failures": 0})
403	        self._append(execution_id, "node_completed", {"node_id": node_id, "output": output, **context})
404	
405	    def _fail_node(self, execution_id: str, workflow: Workflow, state: dict[str, Any], node_id: str, reason: str) -> None:
406	        by_id = {node.id: node for node in workflow.nodes}
407	        retries = by_id[node_id].retries or 0
408	        container, context = self._node_container(workflow, state, node_id)
409	        entry = container["attempts"].setdefault(node_id, {"attempt": 1, "failures": 0})
410	        entry["failures"] += 1
411	        self._append(execution_id, "node_failed", {"node_id": node_id, "attempt": entry["attempt"], "reason": reason, **context})
412	        if entry["failures"] <= retries:
413	            entry["attempt"] += 1
414	            self._append(execution_id, "node_retried", {"node_id": node_id, "attempt": entry["attempt"], "reason": reason, **context})
415	        else:
416	            state["failed_nodes"].append(node_id)
417	            self._terminate(execution_id, state, "retries_exhausted", {"node_id": node_id})
418	
419	    def _ready_tasks(self, workflow: Workflow, state: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
420	        bodies = workflow.loop_bodies()
421	        body_members = set().union(*bodies.values()) if bodies else set()
422	        satisfied = set(state["completed_nodes"]) | set(state["skipped_nodes"])
423	        ready = [
424	            node.id
425	            for node in workflow.nodes
426	            if node.kind == "task"
427	            and node.id not in body_members
428	            and node.id not in satisfied
429	            and set(node.depends_on) <= satisfied
430	        ]
431	        by_id = {node.id: node for node in workflow.nodes}
432	        for loop_id, body in bodies.items():
433	            loop_state = state["loops"][loop_id]
434	            if loop_state["status"] != "running":
435	                continue
436	            iteration = loop_state["iterations"][-1]
437	            iteration_satisfied = set(iteration["completed_nodes"]) | set(iteration["skipped_nodes"])
438	            for node_id in body:
439	                node = by_id[node_id]
440	                if node.kind == "task" and node_id not in iteration_satisfied and set(node.depends_on) <= iteration_satisfied:
441	                    ready.append(node_id)
442	        return sorted(ready)
443	
444	    def _active_loop(self, workflow: Workflow, state: dict[str, Any], node_id: str) -> str | None:
445	        for loop_id, body in workflow.loop_bodies().items():
446	            if node_id in body and state["loops"][loop_id]["status"] == "running":
447	                return loop_id
448	        return None
449	
450	    def _auto_process(self, execution_id: str, workflow: Workflow, state: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
451	        by_id = {node.id: node for node in workflow.nodes}
452	        bodies = workflow.loop_bodies()
453	        body_members = set().union(*bodies.values()) if bodies else set()
454	        completed = set(state["completed_nodes"])
455	        skipped = set(state["skipped_nodes"])
456	        changed = True
457	        while changed:
458	            changed = False
459	            for node in sorted(workflow.nodes, key=lambda item: item.id):
460	                if node.kind == "loop" or node.id in body_members:
461	                    continue
462	                if node.id in completed or node.id in skipped:
463	                    continue
464	                if not set(node.depends_on) <= completed | skipped:
465	                    continue

610	                    iteration["attempts"].setdefault(node_id, {"attempt": 1, "failures": 0})
611	                else:

631	            elif event_type == "iteration_started" and rebuilt is not None:

14	def _reject_non_finite(constant: str) -> Any:
15	    raise ValidationError(f"request body must not contain {constant}")
16	
17	
18	def _assert_finite(value: Any) -> None:
19	    if isinstance(value, float) and not math.isfinite(value):
20	        raise ValidationError("request body must not contain non-finite numbers")
21	    if isinstance(value, dict):
22	        for item in value.values():
23	            _assert_finite(item)
24	    elif isinstance(value, list):
25	        for item in value:
26	            _assert_finite(item)
27

29	class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
30	    service: ChronicleFlow
31	
32	    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: Any) -> None:
33	        return
34	
35	    def _json(self, status: int, value: Any) -> None:
36	        body = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode() + b"\n"
37	        self.send_response(status)
38	        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
39	        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
40	        self.end_headers()
41	        self.wfile.write(body)
42	
43	    def _body(self) -> Any:
44	        content_type = self.headers.get("Content-Type", "")
45	        if content_type.split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower() != "application/json":
46	            raise ValidationError("Content-Type must be application/json")
47	        try:
48	            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
49	            if length < 0 or length > 1_000_000:
50	                raise ValueError
51	            parsed = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length), parse_constant=_reject_non_finite)
52	            _assert_finite(parsed)
53	            return parsed
54	        except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
55	            raise ValidationError("request body must be valid JSON") from error
56	
57	    def _dispatch(self) -> tuple[int, Any]:
58	        path = urlsplit(self.path).path
59	        parts = [part for part in path.split("/") if part]
60	        if self.command == "GET" and parts == ["health"]:
61	            return 200, {"status": "ok"}
62	        if self.command == "POST" and parts == ["workflows"]:
63	            return 201, self.service.create_workflow(self._body(), self.headers.get("Idempotency-Key"))
64	        if self.command == "POST" and parts == ["executions"]:
65	            return 201, self.service.create_execution(self._body(), self.headers.get("Idempotency-Key"))
66	        if len(parts) == 2 and parts[0] == "executions" and self.command == "GET":
67	            return 200, self.service.get_execution(parts[1])
68	        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "executions" and parts[2] == "events" and self.command == "GET":
69	            return 200, {"events": self.service.events(parts[1])}
70	        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "executions" and parts[2] == "checkpoints" and self.command == "GET":
71	            return 200, self.service.checkpoints(parts[1])
72	        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "executions" and parts[2] == "advance" and self.command == "POST":
73	            return 200, self.service.advance(parts[1], self._body(), self.headers.get("Idempotency-Key"))
74	        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "executions" and parts[2] == "claim" and self.command == "POST":
75	            return 200, self.service.claim(parts[1], self._body(), self.headers.get("Idempotency-Key"))
76	        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "executions" and parts[2] == "heartbeat" and self.command == "POST":
77	            return 200, self.service.heartbeat(parts[1], self._body(), self.headers.get("Idempotency-Key"))
78	        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "executions" and parts[2] == "release" and self.command == "POST":
79	            return 200, self.service.release(parts[1], self._body(), self.headers.get("Idempotency-Key"))
80	        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "executions" and parts[2] == "cancel" and self.command == "POST":
81	            return 200, self.service.cancel(parts[1], self.headers.get("Idempotency-Key"))
82	        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "executions" and parts[2] == "recover" and self.command == "POST":
83	            return 200, self.service.recover(parts[1], self._body(), self.headers.get("Idempotency-Key"))
84	        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "executions" and parts[2] == "replay" and self.command == "POST":
85	            return 200, self.service.replay(parts[1])
86	        raise NotFoundError("route was not found")
87	
88	    def _handle(self) -> None:
89	        try:
90	            status, response = self._dispatch()
91	            self._json(status, response)
92	        except ChronicleFlowError as error:
93	            self._json(error.status, {"error": {"code": error.code, "message": str(error)}})
94	        except Exception:
95	            self._json(500, {"error": {"code": "internal_error", "message": "internal server error"}})
96	
97	    do_GET = _handle
98	    do_POST = _handle
99	
100	
101	def main() -> None:
102	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run the ChronicleFlow HTTP service")
103	    parser.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
104	    parser.add_argument("--port", default=8080, type=int)
105	    parser.add_argument("--database", default="chronicleflow.db")
106	    arguments = parser.parse_args()

108	    server = ThreadingHTTPServer((arguments.host, arguments.port), Handler)
109	    print(f"ChronicleFlow listening on http://{arguments.host}:{arguments.port}", flush=True)
110	    server.serve_forever()

20	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workflows (
21	              id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
22	              document TEXT NOT NULL
23	            );
24	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS executions (
25	              id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,

27	              state TEXT NOT NULL

36	            );
37	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS idempotency (

39	              operation TEXT NOT NULL,
40	              response TEXT NOT NULL
41	            );
42	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS checkpoints (
43	              execution_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES executions(id),
44	              sequence INTEGER NOT NULL,
45	              event_sequence INTEGER NOT NULL,
46	              document TEXT NOT NULL,
47	              created_at TEXT NOT NULL,

62	        self.connection.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
63	        try:

65	        except Exception:

import tempfile
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from chronicleflow.errors import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationError
from chronicleflow.service import ChronicleFlow


class ChronicleFlowTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.service = ChronicleFlow(str(Path(self.directory.name) / "test.db"))
        self.workflow = {
            "id": "orders",
            "nodes": [
                {"id": "reserve", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
                {"id": "charge", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["reserve"]},
            ],
        }

    def tearDown(self):
        self.directory.cleanup()

    def test_execution_advances_and_replays(self):
        self.service.create_workflow(self.workflow, "w1")
        created = self.service.create_execution({"id": "run-1", "workflow_id": "orders", "input": {"order": 7}}, "e1")
        self.assertEqual("running", created["status"])
        first = self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {"reservation": 9}}, "a1")
        self.assertEqual(["reserve"], first["completed_nodes"])
        completed = self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {"charge": "ok"}}, "a2")
        self.assertEqual("completed", completed["status"])
        self.assertEqual({"consistent": True, "execution": completed}, self.service.replay("run-1"))

    def test_idempotent_advance_returns_original_result(self):
        self.service.create_workflow(self.workflow, "w1")
        self.service.create_execution({"id": "run-1", "workflow_id": "orders", "input": {}}, "e1")
        first = self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {"value": 1}}, "same")
        repeated = self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {"value": 999}}, "same")
        self.assertEqual(first, repeated)
        self.assertEqual(2, len(self.service.events("run-1")))

    def test_cycle_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "cycle"):
            self.service.create_workflow(
                {
                    "id": "cyclic",
                    "nodes": [
                        {"id": "a", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["b"]},
                        {"id": "b", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["a"]},
                    ],
                },
                "w1",
            )

    def test_key_cannot_be_reused_for_another_operation(self):
        self.service.create_workflow(self.workflow, "shared")
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            self.service.create_execution({"id": "run-1", "workflow_id": "orders", "input": {}}, "shared")


class ConditionWorkflowTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.service = ChronicleFlow(str(Path(self.directory.name) / "test.db"))
        self.workflow = {
            "id": "approval",
            "nodes": [
                {"id": "collect", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
                {"id": "is_vip", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": ["collect"], "path": "customer.vip", "equals": True},
                {
                    "id": "expedite",
                    "kind": "task",
                    "depends_on": ["is_vip"],
                    "run_if": {"condition_id": "is_vip", "expected": True},
                },
                {
                    "id": "standard",
                    "kind": "task",
                    "depends_on": ["is_vip"],
                    "run_if": {"condition_id": "is_vip", "expected": False},
                },
            ],
        }
        self.service.create_workflow(self.workflow, "w1")

    def tearDown(self):
        self.directory.cleanup()

    def start(self, input_data, execution_id="run-1"):
        return self.service.create_execution({"id": execution_id, "workflow_id": "approval", "input": input_data}, f"e-{execution_id}")

    def test_matching_run_if_completes_task_and_skips_other_branch(self):
        self.start({"customer": {"vip": True}})
        self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {"collected": 1}}, "a1")
        state = self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {"fast": True}}, "a2")
        self.assertEqual("completed", state["status"])
        self.assertEqual(["collect", "is_vip", "expedite"], state["completed_nodes"])
        self.assertEqual(["standard"], state["skipped_nodes"])
        self.assertEqual({"is_vip": True}, state["condition_results"])
        self.assertEqual({"collect": {"collected": 1}, "expedite": {"fast": True}}, state["outputs"])
        event_types = [event["type"] for event in self.service.events("run-1")]
        self.assertEqual(
            ["execution_started", "node_completed", "condition_evaluated", "node_skipped", "node_completed", "execution_completed"],
            event_types,
        )
        self.assertEqual({"consistent": True, "execution": state}, self.service.replay("run-1"))

    def test_non_matching_condition_skips_task_and_satisfies_successors(self):
        self.start({"customer": {"vip": False}})
        self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {}}, "a1")
        state = self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {"slow": True}}, "a2")
        self.assertEqual("completed", state["status"])
        self.assertEqual(["expedite"], state["skipped_nodes"])
        self.assertEqual({"is_vip": False}, state["condition_results"])
        self.assertNotIn("expedite", state["outputs"])
        self.assertEqual({"slow": True}, state["outputs"]["standard"])

    def test_missing_path_evaluates_to_false(self):
        self.start({"customer": {}})
        self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {}}, "a1")
        state = self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {}}, "a2")
        self.assertEqual({"is_vip": False}, state["condition_results"])
        self.assertEqual(["expedite"], state["skipped_nodes"])

    def test_equals_compares_json_type_and_value(self):
        workflow = {
            "id": "typed",
            "nodes": [
                {"id": "flag", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": [], "path": "flag", "equals": 1},
                {"id": "act", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["flag"], "run_if": {"condition_id": "flag", "expected": True}},
            ],
        }
        self.service.create_workflow(workflow, "w-typed")
        # boolean true is not the JSON number 1, so the condition is false
        self.service.create_execution({"id": "run-t", "workflow_id": "typed", "input": {"flag": True}}, "e-t")
        state = self.service.advance("run-t", {"output": {"ignored": True}}, "a-t")
        self.assertEqual("completed", state["status"])
        self.assertEqual({"flag": False}, state["condition_results"])
        self.assertEqual(["act"], state["skipped_nodes"])
        self.assertEqual({}, state["outputs"])

    def test_auto_processing_completion_returns_state_without_consuming_output(self):
        self.start({"customer": {"vip": False}})
        self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {}}, "a1")
        state = self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {"slow": True}}, "a2")
        self.assertEqual("completed", state["status"])
        again = self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {"extra": 1}}, "a3")
        self.assertEqual(state, again)
        self.assertEqual(6, len(self.service.events("run-1")))

    def test_condition_only_workflow_completes_during_auto_processing(self):
        workflow = {
            "id": "check",
            "nodes": [{"id": "c", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": [], "path": "ok", "equals": "yes"}],
        }
        self.service.create_workflow(workflow, "w-check")
        self.service.create_execution({"id": "run-c", "workflow_id": "check", "input": {"ok": "yes"}}, "e-c")
        state = self.service.advance("run-c", {"output": {"never": "used"}}, "a-c")
        self.assertEqual("completed", state["status"])
        self.assertEqual({"c": True}, state["condition_results"])
        self.assertEqual({}, state["outputs"])
        self.assertEqual({"consistent": True, "execution": state}, self.service.replay("run-c"))

    def test_condition_definition_is_round_tripped(self):
        document = dict(self.workflow, id="approval-copy")
        stored = self.service.create_workflow(document, "w-copy")
        self.assertEqual(document, stored)

    def test_invalid_nodes_are_rejected(self):
        base = [{"id": "c", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": [], "path": "a.b", "equals": 1}]
        invalid_workflows = [
            # unknown kind
            [{"id": "x", "kind": "gate", "depends_on": []}],
            # unknown field on a task
            [{"id": "x", "kind": "task", "depends_on": [], "path": "a"}],
            # condition missing equals
            [{"id": "c", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": [], "path": "a"}],
            # condition with run_if
            [dict(base[0], run_if={"condition_id": "c", "expected": True})],
            # empty path
            [dict(base[0], path="")],
            # empty path segment
            [dict(base[0], path="a..b")],
            # non-string path
            [dict(base[0], path=7)],
            # non-scalar equals
            [dict(base[0], equals=[1])],
            [dict(base[0], equals={"a": 1})],
            # run_if expected not boolean
            [{"id": "t", "kind": "task", "depends_on": [], "run_if": {"condition_id": "c", "expected": 1}}] + base,
            # run_if with unknown field
            [
                {"id": "t", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["c"], "run_if": {"condition_id": "c", "expected": True, "x": 1}}
            ]
            + base,
            # run_if referencing a task
            [
                {"id": "a", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
                {"id": "b", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["a"], "run_if": {"condition_id": "a", "expected": True}},
            ],
            # run_if referencing an unknown node
            [{"id": "t", "kind": "task", "depends_on": [], "run_if": {"condition_id": "ghost", "expected": True}}],
            # run_if condition not listed in depends_on
            [{"id": "t", "kind": "task", "depends_on": [], "run_if": {"condition_id": "c", "expected": True}}] + base,
        ]
        for index, nodes in enumerate(invalid_workflows):
            with self.subTest(index=index):
                with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
                    self.service.create_workflow({"id": f"bad-{index}", "nodes": nodes}, f"w-bad-{index}")


class LoopWorkflowTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.database = str(Path(self.directory.name) / "test.db")
        self.service = ChronicleFlow(self.database)
        self.workflow = {
            "id": "retry",
            "nodes": [
                {"id": "prepare", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
                {"id": "check", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": [], "path": "again", "equals": True},
                {"id": "attempt", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["check"]},
                {
                    "id": "retry_loop",
                    "kind": "loop",
                    "depends_on": ["prepare"],
                    "entry": "attempt",
                    "condition": "check",
                    "max_iterations": 2,
                },
                {"id": "finalize", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["retry_loop"]},
            ],

    def test_invalid_loops_are_rejected(self):
        check = {"id": "check", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": [], "path": "a", "equals": True}
        attempt = {"id": "attempt", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["check"]}

        def loop(**overrides):
            node = {"id": "loop", "kind": "loop", "depends_on": [], "entry": "attempt", "condition": "check", "max_iterations": 2}
            node.update(overrides)
            return node

        invalid = [
            # zero iterations
            [check, attempt, loop(max_iterations=0)],
            # negative iterations
            [check, attempt, loop(max_iterations=-1)],
            # over the limit
            [check, attempt, loop(max_iterations=101)],
            # non-integer iterations
            [check, attempt, loop(max_iterations="2")],
            [check, attempt, loop(max_iterations=True)],
            # unknown field
            [check, attempt, loop(path="a")],
            # missing entry
            [check, attempt, {"id": "loop", "kind": "loop", "depends_on": [], "condition": "check", "max_iterations": 2}],
            # entry references an unknown node
            [check, attempt, loop(entry="ghost")],
            # entry is not a task
            [check, attempt, loop(entry="check")],
            # condition references an unknown node
            [check, attempt, loop(condition="ghost")],
            # condition is not a condition node
            [check, attempt, loop(condition="attempt")],
            # condition outside the body
            [
                check,
                attempt,
                {"id": "other", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": [], "path": "b", "equals": 1},
                loop(condition="other"),
            ],
            # entry depends back on the loop
            [
                check,
                {"id": "attempt", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["check", "loop"]},
                loop(),
            ],
            # loop depends on a body member
            [check, attempt, loop(depends_on=["check"])],
            # outside node depends on a body member
            [check, attempt, loop(), {"id": "tail", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["attempt"]}],
            # nested loop inside the body
            [
                check,
                attempt,
                loop(),
                {"id": "inner_attempt", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["loop"]},
                {
                    "id": "inner",
                    "kind": "loop",
                    "depends_on": [],
                    "entry": "inner_attempt",
                    "condition": "check",
                    "max_iterations": 1,
                },
            ],
            # overlapping loop bodies
            [
                check,
                attempt,
                loop(),
                {
                    "id": "second",
                    "kind": "loop",
                    "depends_on": [],
                    "entry": "attempt",
                    "condition": "check",
                    "max_iterations": 1,
                },
            ],
        ]
        for index, nodes in enumerate(invalid):
            with self.subTest(index=index):
                with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
                    self.service.create_workflow({"id": f"bad-loop-{index}", "nodes": nodes}, f"w-bad-loop-{index}")
